\section{Hypercontractivity --- Products --- Applications}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Products.Applications
\subsection*{Hypercontractivity --- Products --- Applications: Introduction}
Finite-product hypercontractivity bounds the stability of small events and the stable influences of Boolean functions. Quantitative KKL inequalities and Friedgut junta approximation follow with explicit dependence on the minimum atom mass.

\subsection*{Hypercontractivity --- Products --- Applications: Results}

\begin{theorem}[Stability as a noisy squared norm]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.product_stability_sq_eq_norm_noise_sq}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.component, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.condExp, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.condExp_selfAdjoint, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect_const_mul, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect_sum, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.mass, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.noise, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.norm, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.stability, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomizationAux.component_noise}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p214-b007}
\difficulty{5}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $c\in\mathbb R$, and $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$. Then $\operatorname{Stab}_{c^2}(f)=\|T_cf\|_{2,P}^2$. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $E_Uh(x)=\mathbb E_P[h(X)\mid X_U=x_U]$ for $X\sim P$ and $U\subseteq[n]$; $h_S=\sum_{U\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|U|}E_Uh$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ (the Hoeffding--Efron--Stein components); $T_a h=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}a^{|S|}h_S$ for every real rate $a$; $\|h\|_{p,P}=(\mathbb E_P|h|^p)^{1/p}$ for $p>0$; $\operatorname{Stab}_a(h)=\mathbb E_P[hT_a h]$. The powers indexed by subset cardinalities are natural powers, including $0^0=1$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $P$ be a finite product probability space, let $A$ be an event in its product
outcome space, and let $p>0$. Then the squared $p$-moment norm of its indicator is
$\|\mathbf 1_A\|_{p,P}^{2}=\Pr_P(A)^{2/p}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Event stability from an atom bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.product_smallSet_expansion}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.AtomBound, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.indicator, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.mass, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.noise, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.noise_norm_one_le, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.norm, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.prob, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.stability, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.product_hypercontractivity, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.product_indicator_norm_sq, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.product_stability_sq_eq_norm_noise_sq}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p264-b001}
\difficulty{6}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$ with every coordinate atom at least $0<\lambda\le1$, and let $q\ge2$ and $0\le\rho\le\lambda^{1-2/q}/(q-1)$. For every event $A\subseteq\Omega$, $\operatorname{Stab}_\rho(\mathbf1_A)\le\Pr_P(A)^{2-2/q}$. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $E_Uh(x)=\mathbb E_P[h(X)\mid X_U=x_U]$ for $X\sim P$ and $U\subseteq[n]$; $h_S=\sum_{U\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|U|}E_Uh$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ (the Hoeffding--Efron--Stein components); $T_a h=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}a^{|S|}h_S$ for every real rate $a$; $\operatorname{Stab}_a(h)=\mathbb E_P[hT_a h]$; $\Pr_P(A)=\mathbb E_P\mathbf1_A$, where $\mathbf1_A$ is $1$ on $A$ and $0$ elsewhere. The powers indexed by subset cardinalities are natural powers, including $0^0=1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Stable influence as a noisy norm]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.product_stableInfluence_eq_sq_norm_noise_laplacian}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect_const, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect_const_mul, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.laplacian, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.mass, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.noise, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.norm, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.parseval, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.stableInfluence, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomizationAux.component_laplacian, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomizationAux.component_noise}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $P$ be a finite product probability space with $n$
coordinates, and let $\rho\ge 0$. For every real-valued function $f$ on its outcome
space and every coordinate $i$, $\rho I_i^{(\rho)}(f)=\|T_{\sqrt{\rho}}L_i
f\|_{2,P}^{2}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Absolute Residual Moment Identity]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.product_boolean_residual_abs_expect}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.IsBoolean, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.condExp, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.condExp_comp, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.condExp_selfAdjoint, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect_const, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect_const_mul, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.mass, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.mass_sum}
\difficulty{5}
Let $P$ be a finite product probability space with strictly positive coordinate weights,
let $f$ take values in $\{-1,1\}$ at every point, and let $S$ be a set of coordinates.
The expectation of the absolute residual from conditioning on $S$ equals the second
moment of that residual: $\mathbb E_P|f-E_Sf|=\mathbb E_P(f-E_Sf)^2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Laplacian moments bounded by influence]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.product_laplacian_abs_moment_le_influence}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.IsBoolean, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.influence, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.laplacian, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.mass, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.product_boolean_residual_abs_expect}
\difficulty{5}
Let $P$ be a finite product probability space, let $f$ take values in $\{-1,1\}$ at
every product outcome, and choose a coordinate $i$. For every real $p$ with $1\le
p\le2$, the expectation of the $p$th absolute moment of the coordinate Laplacian is at
most the influence of that coordinate: $\mathbb E_P|L_i f|^p\le I_i(f)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Stable influence from norm contraction]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.product_stableInfluence_le_of_norm_noise_laplacian_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.IsBoolean, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.influence, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.laplacian, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.mass, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.noise, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.norm, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.stableInfluence, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.product_laplacian_abs_moment_le_influence, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.product_stableInfluence_eq_sq_norm_noise_laplacian}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $P$ be a finite product probability space with $n$
coordinates, and let $q,\rho\in\mathbb{R}$ satisfy $q\ge 2$ and $\rho\ge 0$. Let $f$ be
a real-valued function on the outcome space taking values in $\{-1,1\}$, and let $i$ be
a coordinate. If $\|T_{\sqrt{\rho}}L_i f\|_{2,P}\le\|L_i f\|_{q/(q-1),P}$, then $\rho
I_i^{(\rho)}(f)\le I_i(f)^{2-2/q}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Product stable-influence estimate]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.product_stableInfluence}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.AtomBound, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.IsBoolean, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.influence, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.laplacian, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.stableInfluence, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.ProductAux.noise_norm_two_le, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.product_hypercontractivity, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.product_stableInfluence_le_of_norm_noise_laplacian_le}

\difficulty{5}
Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $P$ be a finite product probability space with $n$
coordinates, and let $\lambda,q,\rho\in\mathbb{R}$ satisfy $0<\lambda$, $\lambda\le 1$,
$q\ge 2$, $\rho\ge 0$, and $\rho\le \frac{1}{q-1}\lambda^{1-2/q}$. Suppose every
coordinate atom has probability at least $\lambda$. For every function $f$ taking values
in $\{-1,1\}$ and every coordinate $i$, $\rho I_i^{(\rho)}(f)\le I_i(f)^{2-2/q}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourth-moment stable-influence bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.product_stableInfluence_four}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.AtomBound, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.IsBoolean, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.component, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.influence, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.stableInfluence, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.product_stableInfluence}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p255-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p255-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p267-b005
}
\difficulty{4}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$ with every coordinate atom at least $0<\lambda\le1$. For every $f:\Omega\to\{-1,1\}$ and coordinate $i$, $\sum_{S\ni i}(\sqrt\lambda/3)^{|S|}\mathbb E_Pf_S^2\le I_i(f)^{3/2}$. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $E_Uh(x)=\mathbb E_P[h(X)\mid X_U=x_U]$ for $X\sim P$ and $U\subseteq[n]$; $h_S=\sum_{U\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|U|}E_Uh$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ (the Hoeffding--Efron--Stein components); $I_i(h)=\mathbb E_P(h-E_{[n]\setminus\{i\}}h)^2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Product KKL isoperimetric inequality]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.product_kkl_isoperimetric}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.ComparisonAux.kkl_coefficient_eq, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.ComparisonAux.variance_rpow_ratio_le_noisy_total, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteNorms.exists_sq_div_sum_le_of_sum_three_halves, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.AtomBound, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.IsBoolean, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.component, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.influence, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.totalInfluence, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.variance, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomizationAux.totalInfluence_eq_sum_card_components, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.product_stableInfluence_four}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p267-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p097-b006
}
\difficulty{5}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$ with every coordinate atom at least $0<\lambda\le1/2$. If $f:\Omega\to\{-1,1\}$ has positive variance and $a=I(f)/\operatorname{Var}_P(f)$, there is a coordinate $i$ such that $(a^{-1})^2(9/\lambda)^{-a}\le I_i(f)$. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $E_Uh(x)=\mathbb E_P[h(X)\mid X_U=x_U]$ for $X\sim P$ and $U\subseteq[n]$; $h_S=\sum_{U\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|U|}E_Uh$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ (the Hoeffding--Efron--Stein components); $I_i(h)=\mathbb E_P(h-E_{[n]\setminus\{i\}}h)^2$; $I(h)=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}I_i(h)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}|S|\mathbb E_Ph_S^2$; $\operatorname{Var}_P(h)=\mathbb E_P(h-\mathbb E_Ph)^2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Product KKL theorem]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.product_kkl}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.ComparisonAux.kkl_log_parameters, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.ComparisonAux.kkl_scalar_dichotomy, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.ComparisonAux.variance_rpow_ratio_le_noisy_total, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.AtomBound, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.IsBoolean, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.influence, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.totalInfluence, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.variance, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomizationAux.boolean_variance_le_one, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomizationAux.totalInfluence_eq_sum_card_components, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.product_kkl_isoperimetric}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p267-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p267-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p268-b001
}
\difficulty{6}
There is an absolute $c>0$ such that for every $n\ge2$, every product $P$ of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, with every coordinate atom at least $0<\lambda\le1/2$, and every $f:\Omega\to\{-1,1\}$, some coordinate $i$ satisfies $c\operatorname{Var}_P(f)\log n/(n\log(1/\lambda))\le I_i(f)$. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $E_Uh(x)=\mathbb E_P[h(X)\mid X_U=x_U]$ for $X\sim P$ and $U\subseteq[n]$; $I_i(h)=\mathbb E_P(h-E_{[n]\setminus\{i\}}h)^2$; $\operatorname{Var}_P(h)=\mathbb E_P(h-\mathbb E_Ph)^2$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{6}
There is a universal constant $C>0$ such that the following holds. Let $P$ be a finite
product of probability spaces with strictly positive coordinate weights, let
$n\in\mathbb N$, and suppose every coordinate atom has weight at least $\lambda$, where
$0<\lambda\le 1/2$. For every function $f$ taking values in $\{-1,1\}$ and every
$0<\varepsilon\le1$, there are a coordinate set $J\subseteq[n]$ and a function $g$
taking values in $\{-1,1\}$ that depends only on $J$, such that $|J|\le(1/\lambda)^{C
I(f)/\varepsilon}$ and $\Pr_P(f\ne g)\le\varepsilon$, where $I(f)$ is the total
influence of $f$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Comparison Constant Limit at Zero]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.productNormComparisonConstant_asymptotic_zero}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.productNormComparisonConstant}
\difficulty{5}
For each real number $\lambda$, define $C(\lambda)=e$ when $\lambda=1/2$ and
$C(\lambda)=((1-\lambda)/\lambda)^{1/(2(1-2\lambda))}$ otherwise, with real powers
interpreted using the usual real-power convention. As $\lambda$ tends to $0$ through
positive values, $C(\lambda)\sqrt{\lambda}$ tends to $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Comparison Constant Limit at One Half]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.productNormComparisonConstant_tendsto_half}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.ComparisonAux.constant_tendsto_half, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.productNormComparisonConstant}
\difficulty{1}
For each real number $\lambda$, define $C(\lambda)=e$ when $\lambda=1/2$, and
$C(\lambda)=((1-\lambda)/\lambda)^{1/(2(1-2\lambda))}$ otherwise. As $\lambda$
approaches $1/2$ through values satisfying $0<\lambda<1/2$, $C(\lambda)$ tends to $e$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Sharp product small-set expansion]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.product_smallSet_expansion_sharp}

\difficulty{4}
Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $P$ be a finite product probability space with $n$
coordinates, and let $0<\lambda<1/2$. Suppose every coordinate atom has probability at
least $\lambda$, and let $q>2$ and $\rho\ge 0$ satisfy $\rho\le r_q(\lambda)^2$, where
$r_q(\lambda)=\sqrt{\sinh(u/q)/\sinh\bigl(u/(q/(q-1))\bigr)}$ and
$u=\log((1-\lambda)/\lambda)$. Then for every event $A$ in the outcome space,
$\operatorname{Stab}_\rho(\mathbf{1}_A)\le\Pr_P(A)^{2-2/q}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Sharp product stable-influence estimate]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.product_stableInfluence_sharp}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.AtomBound, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.IsBoolean, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.influence, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.laplacian, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.stableInfluence, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.radius_pos_lt_one, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.product_hypercontractivity_sharp, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.product_stableInfluence_le_of_norm_noise_laplacian_le, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.sharpDiscreteRadius}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $P$ be a finite product probability space with $n$
coordinates, and let $\lambda,q,\rho\in\mathbb{R}$ satisfy $0<\lambda<1/2$, $q>2$, and
$\rho\ge 0$. Suppose every coordinate atom has probability at least $\lambda$, and
suppose $\rho\le r_q(\lambda)^2$, where
$r_q(\lambda)=\sqrt{\sinh(u/q)/\sinh\bigl(u/(q/(q-1))\bigr)}$ and
$u=\log((1-\lambda)/\lambda)$. For every function $f$ taking values in $\{-1,1\}$ and
every coordinate $i$, $\rho I_i^{(\rho)}(f)\le I_i(f)^{2-2/q}$.
\end{theorem}
